newsitem.title: UK: Nat.Grid outlines windfall tax case to govt.
newsitem.headline: Nat.Grid outlines windfall tax case to govt.

text.p: Britain's electricity transmission network National Grid Group Plc has made representations to the new Labour government over a proposed one-off "windfall" tax, finance director John Uttley told Reuters.
"We obviously have made all the appropriate representations," Uttley said.
Paymaster General Geoffrey Robinson asked companies to submit comments on the planned levy by the end of May.
The proposed tax, which will be used to fund a three billion stg plan to cut unemployment, is a central plank of the new government's policy and will feature in its first budget on July 2.
Uttley said National Grid felt it was different from other companies because it has paid rebates to customers and was only demerged from regional electricity companies (Recs) in 1995.

"The Recs owned us for that first period, they were really the returns over that period...and as part of that the considerable customer rebate was returned," Uttley said in a telephone interview with Reuters.
The Grid was demerged from the Recs in December 1995 and paid out a rebate of 50 stg to customers
He added that National Grid was "obviously saying there is a difference between us and everybody else."
